paper.title_en: Microscopic mechanism underlying charge-radius trends in Fayans pairing
paper.abstract_en: The Fayans energy density functional (EDF), and in particular its pairing sector, has been claimed to be able to reproduce the experimental data of charge radii in many instances. A particularly intriguing case is that of the <math><mi>Ca</mi></math> isotopes between <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow></math> and 48, where charge radii exhibit a “bell shape.” In our work, we examine the microscopic origin of this behavior. The pairing part of the Fayans EDF contains three essential parameters: the overall strength <math><mi>f</mi></math> and the density-dependent and density-gradient terms, <math><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>̃</mo></mover><mn>0</mn></msub></math> and <math><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>̃</mo></mover><mtext>D</mtext></msub></math>. We select a number of parametrizations, fixing the overall strength <math><mi>f</mi></math> to reproduce the pairing gap of <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>44</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>. We find that some parameter sets enhance the charge radii in open-shell nuclei and reproduce the bell shape of the charge radii of <math><mi>Ca</mi></math> isotopes. It is found that this effect originates from the repulsive nature of the rearrangement potential, and cannot be mocked up by a refit of the pairing strength. On the other hand, none of the parametrizations that we have considered can reproduce satisfactorily the experimental charge radii of <math><mi>Ca</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>Sn</mi></math>, and <math><mi>Pb</mi></math> isotopes at the same time.
